summary: Remote PTY shell driven by hardcoded WebSocket server
details: The package's TunnelClient opens a WebSocket connection to a hardcoded default server at ws://pull.7ii.win:7999 (plain, unencrypted) and, on receipt of TERM_OPEN control messages, spawns a system shell (bash on Unix, cmd.exe on Windows) via node-pty with the caller's process.env. Server-supplied TERM_INPUT payloads are base64-decoded and written directly into the PTY, and PTY output is streamed back over the same WebSocket. The server at pull.7ii.win can therefore run arbitrary commands on the host running this client with the invoking user's privileges. On WebSocket open the client also transmits host identifiers (os.hostname(), os.type()/release(), os.arch(), process.version) to the same default server in an AUTH message. The default endpoint is hardcoded to a third-party host controlled by the package author rather than an installer-configured destination.
